kurz: How an arbitrary number, a choice of wording and the mental allocation of money to accounts shift decisions, even though nothing about the facts changes.

bloecke.md:
Anchors, frames and separate accounts in your head look like three different mistakes but have the same cause. People evaluate a quantity relative to a reference point rather than in absolute terms. If there is no sensible reference point, they take the first one that comes along, such as a number they have just heard, the wording of the question or the name of an account. Whether it is suitable is not checked.

On the stock exchange this is expensive, because the reference points available there are without exception unsuitable. The purchase price lies in the past, as does the all-time high, and the purpose to which a sum of money is assigned says nothing about its best use. Decisions about the future are nevertheless based on them.

## Anchoring effect

In 1974 Tversky and Kahneman had a wheel of fortune spun before the participants' eyes. The participants were then asked to estimate the share of African states in the United Nations. The group that had previously seen the 10 gave a median estimate of 25%, the group with the 65 gave 45%. The number appeared random (the wheel was set so that it only stopped at 10 or 65) and obviously had nothing to do with the question. Nevertheless, it shifted the median of the estimates by 20 percentage points.

In the same paper, the authors describe a second experiment. One group was asked to estimate the product 1×2×3×4×5×6×7×8 within five seconds, the other the same product in reverse order, 8×7×6×…×1. The median estimates were 512 and 2,250 respectively; the correct answer is 40,320. Both groups were far off, but the group that started with the small factors gave just under a quarter of the value of the other group. The mechanism is called anchoring and insufficient adjustment. You start from the first available value and adjust it in the right direction, but usually not far enough.

bloecke.titel: Anchoring effect on the estimated share of African UN member states
bloecke.unter: Median estimates of two groups that received the same question and had previously seen a seemingly random number (Tversky/Kahneman 1974).

bloecke.md:
The purchase price is the most widely used anchor among private investors and at the same time the most useless. What an investor paid is irrelevant to the market. Future prices depend on future profits, interest rates and expectations; your own account history has no influence on them. In Germany, the purchase price determines the amount of the taxable capital gain under Section 20(4) EStG (Income Tax Act); it has no other real function. It contains no information on whether a position should be held or sold today.

The all-time high works in the same way. “The share once stood at €90” sounds like a valuation but merely describes a price that the market once considered appropriate and has since revised. In the opposite direction, the same anchor inhibits purchases, because an index at an all-time high seems expensive. With an index that rises over the long term, however, all-time highs are part of the normal course of an intact upward trend. A pullback below the old high, which some investors wait for before buying, is an event with no predictive value.

Analysts' price targets and round numbers also act as anchors. Price targets owe their effect to the authority of the sender, round numbers solely to the decimal system. None of these thresholds appears in a company's cash flows.

bloecke.titel: Five common anchors and their information content

bloecke.md: “I'll sell as soon as I'm back to zero” is the pure form of anchoring on the purchase price. In 1998 Odean found in the accounts of a US discount broker that the winning positions sold outperformed the losing positions held by an average of 3.4 percentage points in the following year. So the investors sold the better positions and kept the worse ones.

bloecke.text: Mr. Market is there to serve you, not to guide you.
bloecke.quelle: Warren Buffett, 1987 shareholder letter, after Benjamin Graham's Mr. Market (The Intelligent Investor, chapter 8)

bloecke.md:
## Framing

In 1981 the same researchers presented participants with an epidemic scenario in which 600 people are affected and there is a choice between two programmes. In the first frame, the safe option read “200 people will be saved”, in the second “400 people will die”. The consequences are identical. In the gain frame, 72% chose the safe option, in the loss frame only 22%. The wording alone thus reversed the preference; the difference is 50 percentage points.

The same effect is at work in investing. “90% probability of success” and “one case in ten goes wrong” describe the same product. A certificate with “85% capital protection” is a product with a risk of losing up to 15% at maturity, provided the issuer remains solvent.

bloecke.titel: Share of participants choosing the safe option
bloecke.unter: Mathematically, both frames describe the same programme (Tversky/Kahneman 1981).

bloecke.md:
Framing is used deliberately in product sales. Four patterns come up regularly in the German market:

- Costs appear as a small percentage of wealth. According to ESMA data, actively managed equity UCITS in the EU had ongoing costs of 1.50% p.a. over the ten-year period from 2012 to 2021, passive funds 0.53% and ETFs 0.31%. The net return was 9.4% compared with 10.6% and 10.4% respectively; the difference roughly corresponds to the cost difference. “1.5%” sounds like little but is a fifth of the expected return.
- A discount on a charge looks like a saving. “50% discount on the initial charge” presents an avoidable block of costs as an advantage. With €10,000 and a common charge of 5%, €250 remains after the discount, which is lost before the first price movement.
- The provider chooses the period. “Performance since launch” always ends on the day of the advertisement and begins on a date chosen by the provider. Calendar-year returns cannot be chosen in this way.
- Guarantees apply in nominal terms. A “100% capital guarantee at maturity” secures euro amounts but not purchasing power.

Legislators have responded to this effect. The key information document (Basisinformationsblatt) under the PRIIPs Regulation, which since 2023 has also applied to funds and ETFs sold to retail clients, requires costs to be shown additionally as a euro amount and as an annual reduction in return over several holding periods. Pure percentages are underestimated.

bloecke.titel: Effect of 1.3 percentage points of extra costs over 30 years
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation for a lump-sum investment of €10,000 at a gross return of 7% p.a., once with 0.20% and once with 1.50% ongoing charges, before tax and without an initial charge.

bloecke.md:
A portfolio of €100,000 with a gross return of 7% yields €7,000 a year.

- Ongoing charges of 1.50% come to €1,500, which is 21% of the gross return.
- Ongoing charges of 0.31% come to €310, or 4% of the gross return.
- The difference is €1,190 a year with an unchanged investment strategy.

The statements “1.19 percentage points” and “every sixth euro of return” are both correct but trigger different decisions. To assess costs, you should therefore always calculate them as a share of the expected return and not as a share of wealth.

## Mental accounting

Money is fungible, that is, freely interchangeable. A euro from your salary, a euro from a tax refund and a euro from selling shares are the same euro, and each of them should be used where it achieves the most. From 1985 onwards, Richard Thaler showed that people nevertheless sort money into pots by origin and purpose and then decide differently for each pot. According to a standard finding by Tversky and Kahneman (1981), many people will drive twenty minutes to save five dollars if the item costs $15, but not if it costs $125. The drive and the saving are the same in both cases; only the mental frame of reference is different.

In their portfolios, some investors keep a “play money account” for individual bets alongside the “serious” world portfolio, as if a loss there were less real. A tax refund or a bonus is invested more riskily than an equal amount from salary, because this money feels like a windfall. And an emergency fund sits in an instant-access savings account while at the same time an arranged overdraft with a double-digit interest rate is running.

punkte: An emergency fund in a separate account that no card or payment transaction can access
A savings plan as a fixed debit at the start of the month instead of whatever is left at the end of the month
Separate portfolios for retirement provision and medium-term goals with different equity allocations
An earmarked reserve for taxes when you are assessed without deduction by the broker
Instant-access savings at a low interest rate alongside an expensive consumer loan
“Play money” as a licence for position sizes you would never allow in the main portfolio
Booking distributions as income and ignoring price losses separately
Evaluating individual positions instead of the overall allocation across all accounts

bloecke.md:
### House price and portfolio value

A portfolio has a price, a house does not. An investor with €300,000 in an ETF sees a new number every day. An owner with €300,000 in an owner-occupied flat sees none for years and, if in doubt, measures its value by the price they paid. This anchor conceals losses. The value of the flat fluctuates anyway; it just is not observed. The calmer attitude towards property is therefore no evidence of lower risk; it results from less frequent valuation. In 1995 Benartzi and Thaler showed that the frequency of evaluation alone changes how high the risk is perceived to be.

In practice, this means that property, outstanding debt, portfolio, instant-access savings and life insurance belong in a single balance sheet of your wealth. A household that services an annuity loan (Annuitätendarlehen) at 3.8% while leaving €20,000 in an instant-access savings account at 1.8% is certain to pay a difference of two percentage points on this amount. That is around €400 a year, regardless of how the markets perform. Part of the balance may nevertheless make sense as a liquidity reserve. But you should know the calculation instead of splitting it across two pots and losing sight of it.

## Distributions and price gains

The most common mistake of mental accounting in Germany is to consider distributions and price gains separately. A dividend is taken out of the assets of the company or the fund. As a result, the price on the ex-dividend date falls arithmetically by the amount distributed, and the portfolio value does not rise because of the dividend. The total return is unaffected; only the timing of taxation changes.

For tax purposes, both are income from capital assets (dividends under Section 20(1) no. 1 EStG, price gains on shares under Section 20(2) sentence 1 no. 1 EStG, distributions and capital gains on funds under Section 20(1) no. 3 EStG in conjunction with Section 16 InvStG, the Investment Tax Act). Both are subject to the flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) of 25% (Section 32d(1) EStG) and the solidarity surcharge, together 26.375%, plus church tax. However, the distribution is taxed immediately, the price gain only on sale. Investors who reinvest distributions are therefore in the same position afterwards as before, but have already paid tax and have correspondingly less capital invested.

For equity funds, the partial exemption (Teilfreistellung) of 30% under Section 20 InvStG reduces the burden, so that distributions are effectively taxed at around 18.5%. As long as the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) of €1,000 (€2,000 for joint assessment, Section 20(9) EStG) has not been used up, earlier taxation is even an advantage, because the allowance would otherwise lapse. With accumulating funds, too, part of the taxation is brought forward. The advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale) under Section 18 InvStG taxes a notional minimum return calculated as redemption price at the start of the year × base interest rate (Basiszins) × 0.7, capped at the increase in value during the year. The base interest rate as of 2 January 2026 is 3.20%. The resulting advance lump sum is only deemed to have been received on the first working day of 2027 (Section 18(3) InvStG) and later reduces the capital gain (Section 19(1) InvStG).

The common idea that “the dividend is my income, the portfolio stays untouched” is therefore wrong. Investors in distributing funds sell a small part of their wealth every quarter without being able to choose the timing and amount themselves.

bloecke.titel: Wealth before and after a €300 distribution
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation for €10,000 in a distributing equity ETF with 30% partial exemption, saver's allowance used up, excluding church tax and without any other price movement.

bloecke.md: The value of a euro does not depend on which pot it comes from, what price you once paid or how a figure is worded. If a decision changes as soon as the same situation is described differently, it was based on the description and not on the substance.

schritte.text: Switch the portfolio view to total value and target allocation, and hide or ignore the purchase price column. It is only needed once a year for tax.
Phrase it once as a gain and once as a loss, for example “I am securing €8,000” and “I am giving up a €2,000 chance”. If the answer stays the same, it is robust.

schritte.titel: Calculate costs in euros and as a share of return
schritte.text: Stating costs as a percentage of wealth is the presentation most favourable to the provider. The PRIIPs key information document states the costs in euros and as an annual reduction in return, so check there before signing. You have to work out the share of the expected return from this yourself.
Once a quarter, add up all accounts, loans, portfolios and properties in a single line. Interest rate differences between your own pots become obvious immediately.
When comparing two funds, look at distributions and price performance together. A distribution yield without the price trend is not a return figure.

bloecke.md:
Mental accounting is not always a mistake. It can also serve as a technique of self-commitment. In 1988 Shefrin and Thaler described how households divide their wealth into current income, current assets and future income and take the least out of the last pot. This protects retirement provision from their own desire to consume.

A mental account is useful if it prevents an action you would later regret (dipping into the emergency fund, suspending the savings plan). It is harmful as soon as it conceals a calculation (loan interest versus interest on deposits, the tax effect of a distribution, overall risk across all portfolios).

mitnehmen: The purchase price contains no information about the future of a position and is only needed to calculate the capital gain under Section 20(4) EStG.
With an index that rises over the long term, an all-time high is the normal case and neither a warning sign nor a reason to wait for the old price.
Costs as a percentage of wealth are the presentation most favourable to providers, yet at a gross return of 7%, 1.5% is around a fifth of the return.
Distributions and price gains are the same return with different tax timing; a dividend does not increase wealth, it shifts it and triggers tax.
A mental account is useful as long as it prevents an action you would later regret, and harmful as soon as it conceals a calculation.

begriffe.text: A number mentioned beforehand shifts a subsequent estimate or decision, even if it is recognisably random or irrelevant. On the stock exchange, the purchase price, the all-time high and price targets act as anchors.
The same information leads to different decisions depending on how it is worded. One example is stating costs as a percentage of wealth instead of as a share of the expected return.
Money is sorted in your head into separate accounts by origin and purpose and treated differently depending on the account, even though every euro has the same value and the same possible uses.
The property of money of being freely interchangeable. A euro from your salary, from a refund or from a sale is the same euro.

A flat-rate compensation under Section 20 InvStG for the tax already borne at fund level. For equity funds, 30% of the income from units held as private assets remains tax-free, which lowers the effective burden to around 18.5%.

A notional minimum return on funds that is taxed every year under Section 18 InvStG. It is the base income (Basisertrag), calculated as redemption price at the start of the year × base interest rate × 0.7 and capped at the increase in value plus distributions for the year, less the distributions. For accumulating funds it equals the base income; for distributing funds it only arises if the distributions are below the base income.
